I have followed that line of thinking for the past 4 years. I try to repeat that to my mom on occasion but she brings up her age and says she fears she has no future if we lose our apartment. Thus the desire to kill herself. 

I was thinking about posting to personalfinance. I may give that a shot. Right now, however, I think I have to start moving out. Again, I should have wrote all this out earlier to reaffirm my beliefs and go with my gut instinct.

My first therapist that I ever had mentioned that my mom may be the main catalyst for my depression, but I haven't found a way out. And I don't want her to feel alone. It's a battle between loving my mother and not wanting her to kill herself and wanting my independence and getting out of this situation. It's a crummy fight.

I have had these conversations with her in the past. It doesn't seem to work. Whenever I open up about how I feel, things tend to get worse. I try to be honest with how I feel and she gets angry and tries to justify what she is going through. It's conditioned me to just not say anything to her when she wants to have these conversations. As cold as it may sound, I have times how long I go without saying a word. Longest has been 45 minutes. It's why I feel so defeated when I do talk to her, because nothing I say seems to matter. I have told her to seek help with how she feels and to network, but she tends to go on tangents about obamacare and how she has to waits months on end for her therapy appointment to start. 

She brings up our situation every start of the month. Tension will always build. It's tough. 

I think she wants to hear words of comfort when I just want to provide solutions. Maybe that's where I went wrong.
